title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: New competitive threat; no direct past data, but one past week with competitor entry saw x0.22, though during a holiday. Noise-adjusted effect of competitors is uncertain. Apply modest downside.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.6. No events are scheduled. The price increase to $5.20 (+3.4%) is above regular but not a promotion. Past promotions show a median uplift of x1.18, but the noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0, indicating no lasting effect. The competitor opening across the street is a new, untested demand risk. This could reduce sales, but evidence is thin. A single past week with a competitor entry (2026-06-15) saw a drop to x0.22, but that was during a holiday. No other data supports this. The classical model suggests no effect, consistent with noise-adjusted history. The downside risk is real but uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0. No upward drivers. The baseline’s uncertainty is already well-calibrated.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 51.3 | 10%-90%: 3.9 - 50.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
